 PM Modi to open 7.5-km stretch of Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line on Nov 13
 SECTIONS PM Modi to open 7.5-km stretch of Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line on Nov 13 ET Bureau Last Updated: Nov 03, 2026, 08:05:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch of Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line. The inauguration will take place on November 13, marking a significant expansion of the metro network. This will increase Namma Metro’s operational network to 103.6 km, making it the second-largest in India. The Pink Line connects Kalena Agrahara in the south to Nagawara on the Outer Ring Road.
 PTI Prime Minister Narendra Modi Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere stretch of Bengaluru Metro ’s Pink Line on November 13, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Tuesday.
 During the visit, the Prime Minister will travel from Tavarekere to the IIMB–Bilekahalli station to formally flag off commercial operations, Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya stated in a post on X.
The opening will take Namma Metro’s total operational network to 103.6 km, crossing the 100-km threshold and establishing Bengaluru as India’s second-largest metro network after Delhi, he added. 
The upcoming section is part of the 21.25-km Pink Line linking Kalena Agrahara (Gottigere) in the south to Nagawara on the Outer Ring Road.
“We will build on this momentum and work towards our target of expanding the Metro network to 170 km by 2027,” Gowda said.
 Live Events
 Highlighting the network's expansion, Surya noted that the operational line has grown nearly fifteenfold from just 7 km in 2014, adding over 96 km in the past decade. He credited the Centre's infrastructure push for accelerating urban mobility projects aimed at decongesting the city.
 The announcement follows a joint trial run conducted in September by Gowda, Surya, Bengaluru South MLA M Krishnappa, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Managing Director PC Jaffer, and other senior officials.
